subject: SOC2 SIG: Vulnerability Triage Playbook — 48hr Rapid-Fix Commit Summary
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@heliobank.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: sec@heliobank.com
Date: 2026-09-08T08:13:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SOC2/SIG evidence for 48hr triage SLA and remediation window

Hi Tessa,

Following up from our vendor intake, HelioBank's SOC2 auditor is asking for a concise description of Redwood's 48-hour triage and rapid remediation commitments for critical CVEs (CVSS 9.0+). They specifically requested:

- A short playbook that shows the steps from detection to patch/deploy for critical findings.
- Evidence links for at least two recent incidents showing the 48hr triage window and an RFC/patch commit.
- Scan cadence and how exceptions are handled (hotpatch, backport, compensating control).

Can you provide a single PDF and any links we can hand to the auditor this week? Our audit kickoff is Tue 2026-09-15 and they want pre-read material.

Thanks,
Maria
Security Operations | HelioBank
From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: SOC2/SIG evidence for 48hr triage SLA and remediation window

Kim / Ben — forwarding HelioBank's ask. Short timeline: they want pre-read by 2026-09-15. I attached a draft playbook (remediation-playbook-48hr.pdf) and the scan cadence matrix (scan-schedule-2026Q3.xlsx).

High-level approach in the PDF:
- Detection: automated vuln scan + telemetry alert -> initial triage within 2 hours.
- Classification: security severity + exploit maturity -> critical tag if CVSS >= 9 or active exploit.
- Containment: apply temporary WAF rules / remove access where applicable within 6 hours.
- Remediation: patch backport or hotfix; target commit to internal repo within 48 hours for critical (exceptions documented).
- Validation: post-deploy scan and smoke tests; evidence saved to the SIG evidence drive.

Questions for you both:
1) Ben — can you add two incident exemplars (links + timestamps) that show the 48hr commit?
2) Kimberly — can you confirm exception handling language (hotpatch vs SLA exception) and the compensating control template?

I'll coordinate final packaging and DocuSign acceptance letter if they want an attestation.

Thanks,
Tessa
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: SOC2/SIG evidence for 48hr triage SLA and remediation window

Tessa — I pulled two representative cases and added them to the drive links in the draft:

- CVE-2026-3154: detection 2026-04-22T02:10Z -> triage flagged critical at 02:45Z -> code commit (hotfix branch) 2026-04-22T18:00Z -> production deploy 2026-04-23T01:20Z (total time ~23 hours). Evidence: cve-2026-3154-fix-patch.diff + deploy logs (drive link).
- CVE-2026-1287: detection 2026-06-09T11:05Z -> triage 11:40Z -> patch landed 2026-06-10T08:50Z -> validated 2026-06-10T13:10Z (total time ~26 hours).

I also included commit hashes and the smoke-test output. Note: both used the emergency patch flow (no SLA exception required). I left redactions for internal hostnames in the artifacts.

Kimberly — for exceptions: we classify three exception lanes (planned backport >48h, third-party dependency >48h, and legal/compliance hold). For each lane we include compensating controls: temporary traffic filtering, targeted token rotation, and monitoring retention extension. Can you confirm the templated wording in section 3 of the PDF?

Ben
Senior Vulnerability Engineer, Redwood
From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@heliobank.com>, sec@heliobank.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-09T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC2/SIG evidence for 48hr triage SLA and remediation window

Maria — attaching the requested materials for your SOC2/SIG pre-read. Attached:
- remediation-playbook-48hr.pdf (walkthrough + playbook steps + exception lanes)
- scan-schedule-2026Q3.xlsx (scheduled internal and external scans, roles, and retention windows)
- cve-2026-3154-fix-patch.diff (redacted patch + commit hash reference)

Quick summary of commitments we documented for SIG/SOC2:
- Triage: initial acknowledgement and classification within 2 hours of detection for criticals.
- Rapid fix: target code commit for production hotfix <=48 hours for critical CVEs, with two exemplar incidents attached.
- Exceptions: documented exception lanes (backport, external dependency, legal hold) — compensating controls applied and logged; exceptions require VP-level approval and are surfaced to auditors with a documented remediation plan.
- Evidence: all artifacts uploaded to a read-only drive link and retained for 2 years (see link).

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/sig/HelioBank/remediation-playbook-48hr
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/0abc1234 (optional attestation envelope if HelioBank needs a signed letter)

If you want a 15-minute walkthrough for the auditors next week, Ben and I can join.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
